name: Casey Reas
bio: Casey Reas (born 1972) is an artist and educator who writes software to make images, prints and moving-image works. With Ben Fry he created Processing (2001) at the MIT Media Lab, an open-source programming language for artists and designers that has taught a generation of artists and designers to code. His Process series (2004–2010), collected in Process Compendium, follows Sol LeWitt's wall drawings: each Process is a short text instruction about simple 'elements' and their behaviours, realised in software as a dense, evolving drawing. Since 2018 he has used generative adversarial networks, in Compressed Cinema (2018–2023) and In Silico, and released work on the blockchain, including the Caesuras identity. He is a professor in Design Media Arts at UCLA and co-founded the platform Feral File.
studyNotes: Write the rule in words first. Each Process is a short English text before it is code, so the idea can exist in more than one medium.
Simple elements, complex results. A circle that moves and reacts to touching neighbours is enough to generate a whole field of drawings.
Tools are part of the art. Building Processing, a tool others use, is as significant as any single artwork.
Show the system's variations. Compare two outputs of the same rule side by side; the differences reveal the system.
